title: Securing HDF5 Plugins with Digital Signatures
problem: HDF5 plugins can be misused for malicious routing of calls; currently no systematic mechanism to ensure plugin authenticity and integrity.
motivation: HDF5 is widely used in scientific computing; extensibility via plugins is powerful but introduces security risk; need to systematically improve plugin security.
method: Plugins receive a digital signature—cryptographic proof of authenticity and integrity—when created. Before the system loads any plugin, it verifies this signature to ensure the plugin hasn't been modified. The team evaluates different implementation strategies and measures the tradeoff between performance overhead and security assurance.
key_novelty: The approach verifies HDF5 plugins with digital signatures before they load, ensuring they're authentic and unmodified.
contributions: Digital signature scheme for HDF5 plugin authentication
primary_theme: Digital signature-based security for HDF5 plugins
